issues.title: Bloom filter for joins with one equality key plus non-equality conditions
issues.hypothesis: In q21, the two subquery joins `lineitem l2/l3 ⋈ DELIM_SCAN ON l_orderkey = l_orderkey AND l_suppkey != l_suppkey` (profile: HASH_JOIN 1.10s producing 1.85M rows, plus the sibling join producing 2.93M rows) probe the whole lineitem table against a build side of about 708K distinct (orderkey, suppkey) pairs. No bloom filter gets pushed into the lineitem scan. The reason is in `JoinFilterPushdownInfo::CanUseBloomFilter` (`src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp`:775), which requires `ht->conditions.size() == 1`, and these joins have two conditions. The join hash table only hashes the equality columns (`equality_predicate_columns`, join_hashtable.cpp:43-60), and `InsertHashes` feeds those same hashes into the bloom filter (join_hashtable.cpp:720). So with exactly one equality condition, the filter is a valid membership test on that key alone, whatever non-equality conditions are also present. A second gate also blocks it: when the build side is a `LOGICAL_DELIM_GET`, `build_side_has_filter` is computed as `IsFiltering(join.children[0])`, i.e. on the probe side (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:304-305). The l2 lineitem scan has no filter, so its join never gets a bloom filter. A delim build side is a de-duplicated set of keys from the outer query. Here it covers about 5% of order keys, so a bloom filter would cut about 60M probe rows to about 3M per subquery scan.
issues.plan: 1) In `CanUseBloomFilter` (physical_hash_join.cpp ~775), replace `ht->conditions.size() == 1` with `ht->equality_predicate_columns.size() == 1` (or count the conditions that are COMPARE_EQUAL / NOT_DISTINCT_FROM), keeping `cmp == COMPARE_EQUAL`. Check that the filter column / condition index pushed is the equality one (conditions are reordered so equalities come first, `ReorderConditions` in `GenerateJoinFilters`), and that `PushBloomFilter`'s use of `ht.conditions[0]` and `NullValuesAreEqual(0)` points at that equality condition. 2) In `JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters` (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:303-308), when the rhs is a `LOGICAL_DELIM_GET`, set `build_side_has_filter = true`, or `IsFiltering(children[0]) || <the delim side is a distinct set>`. The existing `probe_larger_then_build` check (estimated probe cardinality > HT count) still prevents wasted builds. Make sure min/max filters for non-equality conditions behave as before. Run `bench q21` and check in `profile` that the lineitem scans under the delim joins show `BF(l_orderkey)` and far fewer rows.
issues.expected_gain: q21: the two lineitem subquery scans and their probes (about 1.1s + ~0.5s operator time) should shrink sharply. I expect 20-40% lower latency.
issues.generality: Helps any hash join with one equality key plus extra inequality/range conditions (common in rewritten correlated EXISTS/NOT EXISTS subqueries, e.g. TPC-H q21/q22-like and other correlated subqueries with residual predicates), and any correlated subquery decorrelated into a join with a DELIM_GET build side over an unfiltered probe table. It could be slightly slower where the bloom filter rejects little, but the existing SelectivityOptionalFilter turns the filter off adaptively when it doesn't help, and the probe>build check still applies.
issues.risk: Low-medium. Correctness depends on the bloom filter hashing exactly the single equality key in the same way as `BFTableFilter::HashInternal` (both use VectorOperations::Hash on one column). With NOT DISTINCT FROM as the only equality, cmp != EQUAL keeps it excluded. Any mismatch in condition index → wrong results, so verify on queries with mixed conditions.

dispatch: Bloom filter for joins with one equality key plus non-equality conditions
